The Challenge alum Nicole Zanatta welcomed twin daughters Seraphina and Madyson on May 1.  “Becoming their mom has been the greatest blessing of my life, but our journey hasn’t been easy,” Zanatta wrote via Instagram on June 1. “Both of my girls were diagnosed with congenital CMV (Cytomegalovirus), a virus I had never heard of until it became part of our story.” She continued, “Since birth, we’ve spent time in the NICU, attended countless appointments which are still ongoing, undergone testing and started medications. I recently brought them home a week ago, but our journey is far from over. Through every high and low, I choose faith over fear, resilience over doubt, and gratitude for every blessing along the way. I will give my girls every opportunity to thrive. I will always fight for them and advocate for their needs.” According to the Mayo Clinic, CMV is "a condition caused by a common virus.” The CMV virus stays in the body for life once a person is infected and can spread through body fluids, including blood, saliva, urine, semen and breast milk.

Kirk in Grand Theft Auto 6 is out to hunt bigfoot, or the Skunk Ape, or Mr. Mangrove, depending on who's talking about it

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Bigfoot in GTA 6, also known as Skunk Ape or Mr Mangrove, isn't just an Easter egg, but a full blown chain of side quests tied to a character called Kirk, who's obsessively hunting the cryptid through the Floridian swamp. After your character stumbles across Bigfoot's location, you can contact Kirk and help him hunt down the Skunk Ape for good across several missions, in which you find the strange effigies that this creature is leaving behind. All this wraps up with a fairly significant choice, one that harkens back somewhat to the famous bigfoot encounter in Red Dead Redemption.

To start with you'll have to ensure your random encounter with the Skunk Ape, but afterwards you can pursue the quest line pretty straightforwardly. Pick the right choices, and you can get a real cash reward.

For a friendlier form of wildlife, check out how to pet animals in GTA 6.

The Skunk Ape questline in which you help Kirk hunt down a monster he calls "Mister Mangrove" is broken up into several smaller quests and objectives.

This is a questline you can start very early on in GTA 6, all the way in chapter 1 1, and see through to the end in the same chapter. The rewards are pretty significant, assuming you make a certain choice.

To find Bigfoot initially in GTA 6 before starting the Skunk Ape quest, you need to go to the location on the GTA 6 map marked above. Once there, you'll see Bigfoot moving fleeing into the marshland after eating a deer.

It's not mandatory that you follow (or even that you have this encounter for the larger quest), but if you do, you'll be led to an effigy tied to a tree. Examining it for too long causes you to inhale spores from it and pass out.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

To start Kirk's quest "Skunk Apeology 101", go to the Rusty Anchor bar in North Key Lento. On entering through the main doors, look immediately to the right and examine the notice board. There'll be a poster left by Kirk, with a number to call if you've seen the Skunk Ape.

With the number added to your contacts, call Kirk. He'll give you a meeting place and time to start the quest, marked on your map with KK.

Meeting with Kirk and getting some explanatory dialogue, he'll have you hit a stick against a truck to trigger the distant howls of Mr. Mangrove. You'll follow him into the woods (I recommend you equip your flashlight in the equipment tab in the bottom left radial menu).

To find Mr. Mangrove after splitting up, use your Focus Mode when you hear the Skunk Ape howling, and there'll be a ripple effect. Follow those ripples until a chase is triggered, leading to another effigy.

At this point, after studying it, you'll be chased by a strange boar. Don't worry too much about escape – whether it catches you or not, you'll end up back at the car, either because you flee successfully or because you're knocked out and Kirk drags you there. He'll tell you he'll contact you again with the next steps, which will take about half a day in-game.

Kirk tells you that he needs you to find three tree Effigies left behind by Mr. Mangrove. There are actually nine of them in total, but you only need to find three of them. We've marked all their locations on the map above – when you're close, use Focus Mode again to see them through the trees, then use L2/LT to study them.

After completing this, you'll be given another message to wait, as now Kirk has the data needed to track the Skunk Ape down for good.

On meeting back up with Kirk at night, you'll be given a customised tranquilizer rifle and taken up in a helicopter. After flushing out the Skunk Ape, you need to fire several rounds into it. Despite the long range, there's no drop-off or delay on the rifle, so just aim at Mr. Mangrove's centre mass and you should be fine.

Eventually he'll end up in a small encampment. Follow him into the building, and you'll see him pass out. When you try to lift him however, things get weird, as you'll be exposed to the pollen spores he emanates and pass out.

In this questionably hallucinatory experience, you'll now control a frog and have to find flies to eat. There are three different spots to go to where flies congregate over corpses.

Be wary that there are alligators who will try to eat you. Keep your distance, and use Focus Mode to home in on the flies.

Having eaten flies, now you'll become one, obviously. Head back to the shack you found the Skunk Ape in, but now follow the other pier around back to the helicopter (its lights should mark it out). Stay close to Kirk, and you'll hear him talking about a man named Harry Sherrick who disappeared – who actually is Mr. Mangrove, with a valuable QR code tattoo that will lead to open his substantial bank account.

Waking up in the shack with Kirk and the unconscious Mr. Mangrove, you can choose to side with either of them, now knowing that Kirk is fully aware that the Skunk Ape is some transformed human being and is only hunting him to rob him. You can choose to shoot either of them with the dart gun, or neither. Here are the options and what they give you:

No matter what outcome you pick, you get to keep the rifle, a legendary variant "Mister Mangrove" Laird 350 Bolt Action Rifle. That reward, at least, is consistent.

Of the three, the best choice if you want to make money fast in GTA 6 is to shoot Mr. Mangrove. However, if you want to be an ethical criminal, I would shoot neither and let the Skunk Ape have his revenge.

It's heavily implied that Mr. Mangrove is a man named Harry Sherrick who was transformed by swamp spores into a Skunk Ape, similar to the mutated boar that chases you early in the quest chain.

Kirk knows this and has been relentlessly hunting and hounding Sherrick anyway – not to help him, or to reveal the truth to the world, but to simply get access to the tattoo and steal the money. Kirk's a pretty shitty person, simply put, especially as he had no intention of even cutting Jason and Lucia in on the reward.

If you lose track of your new rifle, make sure you know how to store and recover your weapons in GTA 6.

The PS5 triggers are changing how I drive in GTA.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me.

But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.

GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff.

Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles: When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point.

I've been calling this low-speed mode. At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode.

Don't worry, it's not hard to fully gun it either: Just pull the trigger with a little gusto and you're off to the races. This is what the two speeds look like:

This has completely changed how I drive in GTA. I'm already someone who takes these games slowly, but the natural stopping point of the throttle makes this easy and natural—as if Rockstar is not just allowing for a more immersive playstyle, but endorsing it.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's just a different experience than having to manually learn the speed thresholds and intuitively hold the trigger at an exact middle point. This is more like I'm pulling the trigger to one natural stop for "slow", and another for "fast". It's the four-wheeled equivalent of Jason and Lucia's walk (you have to press L3 to enter a jog or sprint), or the default saunter of Red Dead Redemption 2's horses.

I can only recall one other open world game with a similar feature: the older Mafia games had speed limit toggles that automatically prevented cars from surpassing the speed limit. I always liked that, too, but this is more elegant.

It turns out Rockstar's co-branding campaign that insists GTA 6 "plays best on PS5" isn't just marketing. In these months before GTA 6 is a PC game, I really would suggest you play it on a PlayStation for the controller perks alone. And when the time comes, I hope Rockstar goes the extra mile to port these DualSense features to the PC version.

#3828. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

#3827. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#3825. Viola Davis and More Condemn 'George Floyd the Musical' Amid Backlash

Producers of the as-yet-unproduced cast recording of George Floyd the Musical are defending the project amid criticism from Viola Davis, Ahmir “Questlove” Thompson and numerous prominent Broadway stars.

“Busted Broadway seeks to push the limits of what is possible in musical theatre by producing provocative and satirical musical cast albums,” read a Thursday, November 19, statement from New Jersey-based independent music label Busted Broadway. “Our George Floyd the Musical is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It’s a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now.”

The show drew a harsh rebuke via social media when activist and actress Malynda Hale brought to light that Broadway publication Playbill recently ran a job listing for a cast recording session.

“I’m usually not speechless but … yeah,” she said in a Wednesday, November 19, Instagram Reel that flashed the job listing on screen.

Busted Broadway actors sought “comedic singers and musical theater vocal talent” to record and improvise content for George Floyd the Musical. A disclaimer on the job advertisement warned that Busted Broadway’s projects are “too ridiculous, too raunchy and too absurd for the stage.”

“If you are uncomfortable performing offensive material, we ask that you do not submit for this project,” the company requested.

A statement on the Busted Broadway website claimed that the troupe was formed in 2025 to address “a necessity to reinvigorate the barren wasteland of mundane, mediocre musical theatre shows foisted upon audiences today.” Other projects promoted by the theater company include Human Centipede the Musical and Genghis Khan the Musical.

“In an age where entertainment feels increasingly safe, sterile, and insufferably self-serious, Busted Broadway exists to shake the snow globe and remind audiences that laughing at dark humor is not only allowed but necessary,” the site’s About Me page read.

A listing for George the Musical promotes “The $20 Bill that Changed the World” as its tagline, along with a cartoon rendering of three police officers standing over an unconscious Floyd.

Former Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin was convicted of unintentional second-degree murder, third-degree murder and second-degree manslaughter in April 2021 over Floyd’s May 2020 murder. Four police officers confronted an unarmed Floyd for allegedly using a counterfeit $20 bill at a local grocery, before Chauvin physically restrained Floyd and knelt on his neck for nearly 10 minutes, causing Floyd to asphyxiate.

In the wake of George the Musical‘s job listing going viral, many notable figures have condemned the project.

“I mean……WHAAT??!!! I would’ve lived to have been in the room when this one was pitched,” Davis, 61, responded to Hyde’s Instagram video.

Questlove, 55, also expressed disbelief over the project, replying, “OMG!!!!!!!! it took 17 seconds to register. I saw the headline for 4 secs and was like ‘wait they made a broadway play on how he developed those sandwich machin————OH GOD WAIT READ THAT AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!????????'”

Playbill has publicly apologized for running the listing, insisting that it slipped through an internal procedure designed to weed out offensive advertisements.

“Late yesterday afternoon, Playbill Jobs incorrectly approved a job listing that had no place on our site,” a statement read. “Once leadership was alerted, the listing was immediately removed, and we began reviewing and revising our approval processes. We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward. We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.”

Playbill acknowledged the offense caused by its apparent unintentional promotion of George Floyd the Musical “has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet.”

“For that, we are sorry, and are committed to regaining your trust,” the statement concluded.

The ad has been removed from Playbill’s site.

A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light.

I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. But just a short way down the road, moments after blasting past a few panicked pedestrians I'd aggressively robbed of the right of way, it happened again: Without thinking, I'd come to a complete stop at a stop sign.I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety.

Repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette. I'm following other drivers at a reasonable distance when I could be forcing them off the road to save time. I'm diligently staying in my lane when I could be scraping my way up the shoulder at 90 miles an hour. NPC passengers have berated me mid-mission for not driving fast enough because I'm checking both directions before crossing an intersection. Something is wrong with me.

To be entirely clear: I've never had this issue before. As with any other sensible person, my time in the two decades and change that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto have been characterized by a blatant disregard for roadway caution. If I was ever driving safely, it was either by accident or as a sort of affectation—like when you do a crappy posh accent to make fun of the moneyed classes.

But in GTA 6, something is different. Something has shifted in the simulation enough that I'm opting out of vehicular psychopathy without even meaning to—something in the increased visual fidelity and the intensified sense of heft and momentum. Something's stepped across some critical line of verisimilitude, and now I'm instinctively treating its virtual cars like the multi-ton slabs of explosion-propelled metal they're meant to evoke.

Warte uwagi też jest to, jak nagle zmienia się atmosfera w GTA6 po użyciu broni w przestrzeni publicznej. Drastyczna zmiana klimatu. Dziesiątki uciekających NPC. Motyw dźwiękowy. Bardzo sugestywne i niepokojące. https://t.co/ugPYtWYtz1November 18, 2026

And it's not just the cars, either. There's a tweet circulating today from a Polish user who noted how firing a weapon in public feels more dire in GTA 6 than in previous entries, demonstrating the point with a video of panicked beachgoers fleeing en masse as Jason fires a pistol into the air. I can confirm that—perhaps not coincidentally—I've been doing a lot less non-vehicular psychopathy, too.

During in-mission firefights and gang raids, I'm as unphased by the violence on display as I've been by the collective years of videogame combat I've done beforehand. There, it's action movie absurdity. Elsewhere, though, I'm rarely reaching for a firearm. Age is partially to blame: Random acts of simulated violence aren't as titillating at 33 as they were at 12. But the truth is, Rockstar's absurd expenditure of art and animation tech has produced a crime game where firing a gun with no good reason can feel downright criminal.

When there's so much attention dedicated to how characters move and shift their mass, when the world around them is lit so believably and packed with so much detail, the violence you can inflict feels so much more acute. I don't think it's immoral to shoot a gun or drive a car at someone in GTA 6. But I do think it feels queasy—queasy in a way I'm not used to feeling. The uncanny valley isn't new, but being able to empty a weapon into it is.

#3823. It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the big release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either."

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe."

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

Mysterious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reemerged in the wake of GTA 6's release with another leak: This time, they have released what they claim to be a near-complete build of GTA 6 on Xbox from November 2026.

In their post, Cyberleek says they'll drop the one file they've withheld—the main executable—if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. Yeah, we're doing this again. Comments on a now-removed Reddit post say the leaked file is around 200 GB, which is close to the size of GTA 6 on consoles.

Cyberleek says they will release the exe on November 23, no matter what.

"It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons," the posts read.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build—a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar."

Last we heard from Cyberleek was over a month ago, when they were threatening Take-Two with a "dead man's switch", which many took to mean they'd either post major story spoilers or leak the game in its entirety.

We've yet to see confirmation that the build is genuine, but that could come as soon as tonight. If it is, it'll be anywhere between a few days or hours before the executable comes: According to Cyberleek's site, their crypto currently sits at a $1.83 million cap.

#3819. Late MLB Star Pete Rose Posthumously Pardoned by President Trump

President Donald Trump is posthumously pardoning baseball legend Pete Rose, two years after his death.

“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND,” Trump, 80, posted via Truth Social on Thursday, November 19.

The former professional player, whose career spanned more than two decades, died of heart disease at age 83 at his Las Vegas home in September 2024. Prior to his death, Rose pleaded guilty in 1990 to two felony counts of filing false federal tax income returns, for which he served five months in prison.

Rose, the all-time hits leader in Major League Baseball history, became a superstar with the Reds from 1963 to 1978. He would later return to the Reds in 1984 and play the final three seasons of his professional career with the franchise, when he also acted as a player-manager for the team until 1989.

In August 1989, during his final year as Reds’ manager, Rose was permanently banned from baseball after allegations that he gambled on games during his playing career. The accusations suggested Rose placed wagers on games involving his own team.

Rose was subsequently banned from being eligible for the Major League Baseball Hall of Fame, despite being one of the league’s most decorated and beloved players in history. The exclusion of Rose has been a point of contention in the baseball community for decades.

In May 2025, Major League Baseball commissioner, Rob Manfred, reinstated Rose to the MLB, which opened the door for him to be posthumously inducted into the Hall of Fame.

After years of public denial, Rose admitted the allegations against him were true in 2004, but he continued to fight for his reinstatement when he was still alive.

“For me, the thrill wasn’t about the odds. I got involved because I was rooting for my teams — no, believing in my teams. I bet the Reds to win every time. I bet the Phillies to win even though they were huge underdogs and on a losing streak,” he wrote via his 2004 memoir, My Prison Without Bars. “It wasn’t the smart way to bet. But it was my gut feeling … and I always bet with my gut. I never — ever — bet against my teams. If I had, I’d be doubting everything I believed in. And, hell, to my way of thinking, we were going to win every night. You can’t be a competitor and think otherwise.”

Despite his controversial past that eventually led to him being banned from baseball, Rose was remembered by the League after news of his death broke in 2024.

“Major League Baseball extends its deepest condolences to Pete Rose’s family, his friends across the game, and the fans of his hometown of Cincinnati, Philadelphia, Montreal and beyond who admired his greatness, grit and determination on the field of play,” the official MLB account wrote via X at the time. “May he rest in peace.”

While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update.

If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.

#3817. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more."

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

It’s a common practice for celebrity couples to keep their private lives, well private, and it’s no different for Zendaya and Tom Holland. While the two choose to keep things private, they understand the “parasocial investment” fans have in their relationship. However, even big-name directors can’t help sharing funny relationship stories about them, such as dishing about Holland’s funny reaction to seeing Zendaya in The Odyssey, and it’s just too perfect.

Director Christopher Nolan continued to praise Zendaya’s performance when he sat down with Stephen Spielberg during a special screening of The Odyssey. However, this time around he shared what her husband’s reaction was to seeing her play a goddess, and it’s probably not what you think. During the Q&A (via People) in West Hollywood, California, Nolan revealed there was a moment that got a little too real for Holland:

You have his vision of Athena made by Zendaya. I mean, she just gives him this look of disappointment. When Tom Holland saw the film, he’s like, ‘I know that look. Now, Holland did have a front-row seat to watch her work her magic. The spouses may not have shared a scene in The Odyssey, but that doesn’t mean they weren’t together on set. Zendaya previously shared during a Los Angeles special screening Q&A that Holland helped calm her nerves on her first day. Her husband sat off to the side in a corner, reminding her, “You got this.”

Additionally, this isn’t the first time Nolan has praised Zendaya. The scene that reveals Athena in a vision of Odysseus, where she appears as a guide, is so good that Spielberg also sang her praises:

It was wonderful, but she was also kind of a therapeutic companion. She just was there accompanying him. It was great accompaniment. And I thought she was wonderful. I think everybody was wonderful in the movie.

The high praise is valid, as there’s good reason why Nolan chose Zendaya to play the goddess of wisdom. Let’s just hope he doesn’t have to see ‘that look’ again.

#3815. The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the big deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

This is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

#3812. GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

"The decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers."

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop."

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition."

Though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

#3811. Ken Urker's Mom Says He Struggled With Split, Cyber Bullying Before Death

Ken Urker’s mom, Raina Urker, gave a candid insight into her son’s final days.

Speaking to TMZ in an interview shared on Thursday, November 19, Raina said Ken was struggling with his split from ex-fiancée Gypsy Rose Blanchard, 35, as well as “cruel” cyber bullying before he died.

“He would internalize what people said about him on the internet and it bothered him when it was just so cruel,” she told TMZ.

Raina said Ken was particularly concerned about how the negative online commentary would affect his 22-month-old daughter, Aurora, whom he shared with Blanchard.

“It was such cruel things being said about him and that would bother him because of Aurora,” Raina continued. “He didn’t want Aurora to grow up and see these things and, of course, phone calls were coming out from prison and that bothered him.”

Confirming that Ken and Blanchard were not in a relationship at the time of his death, Raina added that the couple’s break up was also weighing heavily on his mind.

“Gypsy and him were going through ins and outs and that bothered him because he very much did not want Aurora to be raised with split parents,” Raina said, adding that a united family unit was something Ken “wanted his whole life.”

“He wanted the parents to be together,” she explained.

Raina also insisted that Ken never would have committed suicide despite the speculation surrounding his death, stating,  “He loved Aurora way too much to have done anything like that.”

News broke in October that Ken was found dead inside a Louisiana home on his 34th birthday.

The investigation into Ken’s death “remains ongoing” after a coroner confirmed he died by accidental overdose.

“The Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of Kenan Urker,” the sheriff’s office told Us in a Monday, November 15, statement. “While we understand the Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office has released updated information regarding the cause of death, our investigation is separate and remains ongoing.”

Authorities added, “At this time, we have no additional information to release. We will provide an update when we reach a point in the investigation where additional information can be shared.”

Earlier on Monday, Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office confirmed that Ken’s cause of death was an accidental overdose.

“The final cause of death has been determined to be accidental poly substance drug toxicity,” a statement read. “The case is now complete, and no further testing is pending.”

Ken had a complicated relationship with Blanchard. The pair were first connected when Ken wrote to her in prison in 2017 and they subsequently became pen pals.

At the time, she was behind bars for her role in the 2015 murder of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard.

Although Ken and Blanchard were engaged in 2018, they called it quits later that same year.

Blanchard went on to marry Ryan Anderson in July 2022 while still incarcerated. She was released in December 2023 but her marriage to Anderson didn’t go the distance. They called it off in the spring of 2024.

In December 2024, the same month her divorce to Anderson was finalized, Blanchard welcomed Aurora with Ken after they reconnected outside of prison.

As a child of the early 2000s, I grew up obsessed with Gilmore Girls and Gossip Girl. These remarkable teen shows were irresistible, and they are how I was introduced to Jared Padalecki and Leighton Meester. So, you can imagine my excitement when I learned that these actors would be leading the rom-com, Guarding Stars, on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule together. So, I had to ask about how they bonded over their time on shows like Gilmore Girls and Gossip Girl, and Padalecki’s G-oriented response hilariously surprised me.

When I brought all this up to Jared Padalecki, who plays actor Jack Stapleton in Guarding Stars, he said he did speak to Meester about their time on The CW and their work on the “G-titled girl shows,” as Padalecki affectionately called them. Elaborating on that hilarious point, the Supernatural star said:

Yeah, we did talk about it here and there. We didn't get into deep, deep detail. But yeah, I also joke that I was in Gilmore Girls; she was in Gossip Girl. Then there's Golden Girls. We were all on the double G titled girl shows. Well, I didn't get to be on Golden Girls, but I wish.

Well, I certainly didn’t see this hilarious point coming. While I’ve always been entertained by the fact that both Jared Padalecki and Leighton Meester were on maybe two of the three most famous [insert name that starts with G] Girl(s) shows around, I didn’t think he’d bring it up. I also didn’t think he’d say he wanted to be on Golden Girls, but now I wish that could have happened somehow.

Anyway, getting back to the Gossip Girl and Gilmore Girls vets working together, Padalecki said their similar experiences of getting their break on major television programs did help them bond on set. In fact, as they filmed Guarding Stars, which is a Christmas flick on the 2026 movie schedule, in the cold, they found themselves discussing how the industry has evolved with some of their other co-stars:

But we did talk about it and just how the industry in general has changed. Especially, there'd be scenes where it was too cold to wait outside in between takes, so they'd have a warming hut for us or a warming room, and having Andie MacDowell there to talk about when she had started and the differences and this and that, and so we would bond about it.

Yeah, this book-to-screen adaptation of Katherine Center’s The Bodyguard is full of veteran actors. I can only imagine the conversations Padalecki, Meester and MacDowell, who plays Padalecki’s mom in the movie, had. Speaking more to that point, the actor told me that he and the Gossip Girl star's similar TV history did really help them work together:

But I think there was just more than talking about it. There was just an understanding when we got to set that she's a technician and she's talented, and she's done hundreds of hours of work. And I think hopefully she thought the same me, so we just hit the ground running. It wasn't like, ‘No, here's how you hit a mark, and here's how you find the lens.’ Like, I knew she knew; she knew I knew. It's like, ‘Cool, let's play. Let's see what the words bring us.’

So, the double-G connection, if you will, really served them well on this. While Meester and Padalecki were never on the same shows, they both broke big through projects that aired on The CW, and having that background helped them get off to a great start in Guarding Stars.

Now, in this new G project the two actors star in, Padalecki plays an actor, and Meester is his bodyguard. However, to maintain their cover with his parents, they have to fake date. It’s a very fun, wholesome, and action-packed movie that’s well worth the time. And if you’re a fan of the “double G-titled girl shows,” you really won’t want to miss it.

With that said, Guarding Stars is available to stream with a Netflix subscription. And if you’d like to stream “the double G-titled girl shows,” you can catch Gilmore Girls and Golden Girls with either a Disney+ or Hulu subscription, and Gossip Girl is streaming for those with an HBO Max subscription.

#3809. GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

"It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps."

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson said the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson said, adding that websites may return in the future.

"I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world."

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore new possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its big heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the new Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

Cyberleek is back. The account behind a trove of unprecedented gameplay footage leaks for Grand Theft Auto 6 prior to its launch this week is once again threatening to release an allegedly working build of the game online, and may have already done so. And yes, the account is once again demanding people mine crypto in order for the build to become playable.

“It is done,” began a new announcement posted on the Cyberleek account’s website on November 19. “CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one â the main executable â held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.”

gta vi cyber leek build out for xbox. only missing the executable. total size: 209GB

There are reports of files for a build floating around, though Kotaku is unable to verify them and whether they are legit. Cyberleek claims to have withheld the executable file needed to actually run the leaked Xbox build, and will only release that last piece if the market cap for the $CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches $15 million. “If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build â a fallback, most likely never required,” the post reads. “Either way: the Xbox build is going out. You remember when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake launched earlier this month on Nintendo Switch 2, and it was running on PC in hours? Well, modders are claiming essentially the same will be happening for Grand Theft Auto 6, a much bigger and more complicated game.

If you're wondering how these games are getting ported so quickly, it's a mixture of people dumping the game files for the public to access and, oftentimes, generative AI coding doing a lot of the grunt work of recompiling.

Just yesterday, Cyberleek (the hacking team or person who leaked GTA 6 files earlier this year) reportedly leaked the GTA 6 Xbox build, giving modders access to the game's release files. That's one important part of the porting process checked off.

The only file Cyberleek says it hasn't dropped is the main executable file, and they say they will release it when their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. However, Cyberleek did say they would drop the exe file on November 23 either way. Even Cyberleek claims "this community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps"

Game modder OptiJuegos notes that GTA 6 is a GDK App, sharing its architecture with Windows and hoped for a dump of the Xbox version just a few days ago so it would run easily on PC, before Cyberleek's dump of the Xbox version.

Por suerte GTA 6 es una APP GDK y comparte casi toda la arquitectura con WindowsEsperemos algun DUMP de la version de XBOX. No hay nada publico en los servidores pic.twitter.com/8V0u3FHXSANovember 18, 2026

Cybersecurity expert VX Underground took a look at the Xbox file dump and reckons it's real, and even reckons it will be playable on the 23rd if the executable file is released. Another X user notes that the dump appears to be missing the "EmbeddedXvd folders that is inside the gameos.xvd" which apparently contain system DLL files, as well as the NT kernel and drivers. Still, this is something modders can work around.

> wake up> take a shit> get out of bed> check beep boop> over 9000 DMs> "SCHMEELI, GTA VI LEAK"> ???> sends link> torrent> ok> look inside> actual assets> huh> squint eyes> look closer> not larphuh, how about that. the cyberleek guy released the full xbox gta 6… pic.twitter.com/1MDrGI97DyNovember 19, 2026

There's nothing to do but wait to see if modders actually will release a port of GTA 6 on PC, but Rockstar is infamously litigious, and emulation is a legally grey area at best, and downright illegal at worst. Emulation tools and recompilers aren't illegal by themselves, but downloading ROMs and game dumps you don't own is a form of copyright infringement, and game companies would argue that it costs them a lot of cash at the end of the day.

#3806. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was October's biggest game in the US, but it wasn't enough to crack 2026's best-selling top 10

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other big-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were new releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a big slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything new, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested."

Ebenzer was at the top of the box office when it arrived in theaters, but the book to screen adaptation didn't make that much money compared to Depp's past projects. Over on the Naughty But Nice Substack, writer Rob Shuter quoted an alleged industry insider, who spoke about how the movie's performance may influence the future of Johnny Depp's career. In their words:

This was Johnny’s test, and he got a C. That’s not good enough for a studio looking to spend a fortune on a franchise. The problem is, it wasn’t a complete disaster. If the movie had totally bombed, everyone could walk away and move on. Instead, these middle-of-the-road numbers leave Hollywood with a difficult decision.

At the time of writing this story, Ebenzer has made $43.4 million on a reported budget of $38 million. Johnny Depp took a huge pay cut to keep at number low, but it wasn't enough to reach huge box office numbers of previous projects like the Pirates of the Caribbean movies. If this source is to be believed, the powers at Hollywood might not be inclined to give him major gigs following how Ti West's new movie did.

Ebenezer's cast has plenty of familiar faces, but Depp has been front and center of the movie's promotional tour. He even showed up at San Diego Comic-Con dressed as Scrooge. Fans have been wondering if the actor might return as Captain Jack Sparrow in another Pirates movie, but according to the same source, that might be less likely after Ebenezer. They claimed:

Pirates is the ultimate prize for Johnny, but Hollywood needs to know audiences still want to see him. Nostalgia alone won’t sell hundreds of millions of dollars in tickets.

We should probably take these quotes with a grain of salt, but it should be interesting to see where/if Johnny Depp appears in another major film production. He returned to acting in Jeanne du Barry, but that was a French film produced outside of the Hollywood machine. While he's got plenty of beloved movies on his resume, it's unclear if moviegoing audiences can get past the Amber Heard ordeal and still want to show up in theaters to see him on the big screen.

Ebenezer is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. We'll have to see how much money it makes deeper into its theatrical run, as well as what projects Johnny Depp signs on for next.

#3804. As Rockstar's alleged "union busting" tribunal hearing comes to a close amid GTA 6 launch, judge pledges to deliver verdict "as quickly as I possibly can"

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can."

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog."

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it."

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

#3803. ‘9-1-1: Nashville’ EP on Possible Deaths After Hostage Twist, Pharaoh Reveal

Nashville’s finest were pushed to the brink during the 9-1-1: Nashville fall finale — and after a kidnapping twist, two beloved characters could be in grave danger.

Warning: Spoilers below from season 2, episode 6 of 9-1-1: Nashville.

“All the main characters are at risk,” showrunner Rashad Raisani exclusively told Us ahead of the Thursday, November 19, episode, teasing that both Fire Captain Don Hart (Chris O’Donnell) and Detective Rogue Kelly (Ryan Phillippe) cannot come out of their predicament “unharmed.”

During the fall finale, titled, “Tears of the Nile,” Rogue’s season-long foe known as “The Pharaoh” gave him 48 hours to figure out what his cryptic “kill the seven” message meant and how to stop his latest attack on Music City.

With the help of Nashville’s first responders, Rogue discovered that the “seven” individuals meant seven firstborn children, who all disappeared on the same night after playing a video game about a pharaoh. The vow for the “death of the firstborn” is the 10th and final plague in the Book of Exodus, following the killer’s modus operandi (MO).

While the seven children were found safely — after their impending doom was livestreamed and a grain silo filled with water with every new viewer — the pharaoh was still on the loose. (One of the kids, who were all connected through their church, was able to describe him to a sketch artist, getting them one step closer to finding his identity.)

During the final moments of the episode, Don stopped to help a man whose car broke down ahead of celebrating his son firefighter Ryan Hart (Michael Provost) and wife Dr. Sam Hart’s (MacKenzie Porter) pregnancy announcement at his home.

Don was drugged and kidnapped. When he woke up there appeared to be a bomb around his neck and he was looking at the pharaoh, a dark-haired man with a scruffy beard. They weren’t alone, however, as Rogue had also been taken and was tied up across from Don.

“We warned you what would happen if you kept interfering but you didn’t listen, did you?” pharaoh told Don. “You thought you denied me the death of the firstborn. You just delayed it. And the only question is, which one of you will it be?”

After pharaoh’s ominous warning, Raisani told Us that fans should be “pretty worried” about the hostage situation.

“This case is going to go to even more twisted places and darker places than it even seems,” he said. “And it’s going to get pretty dark really fast.”

While the executive producer played coy about how Don and Rogue will escape their captor, Raisani confirmed that “definitely we aren’t killing two [characters],” as Don’s sister-in-law, Cammie Raleigh (Kimberly Williams-Paisley) deals with her own villain in 9-1-1 call center supervisor Marcia Zellner (Camryn Manheim).

Scroll down for a breakdown of what’s to come when 9-1-1: Nashville returns in January — including how much danger Cammie is in with her prank caller and if Phillippe is coming back after this season:

“It’s two things. One, is that he warns them from episode two on. He says, ‘Anybody who interferes with my plans, you will be punished. There will be consequences.’ And he’s kind of warned them a couple times,” the showrunner explained. “So now he’s saying, ‘OK, here are the consequences.’”

Additionally, the serial killer warned, “I’m gonna have my death of a firstborn [plague], and you know, big surprise, Don and Rogue are both firstborns.” Raisani added, “His will will be done, and so that’s kind of his ultimate plan was to say, ‘You guys got my way, and now there’s a price.’”

“We always knew who this person would be, but we also didn’t want to let anybody look too innocent because it’s a complex story,” Raisani told Us, noting that while fans have been “clever” in their theories — one of which was that Rogue was actually the killer — the mystery of which characters are “not as innocent or as above board as they seem” is still being unraveled.

He pointed out, “There is a web that’s a little bit more complex than what’s being revealed right now.”

“I didn’t want to be done with him so fast, so that there was no chance on my end that he was going to be the Pharaoh,” Raisani revealed, noting that while someone could die when the show returns, Phillippe’s story as Rogue isn’t done yet.

The executive producer told Us, “I love what Ryan has been on the show and what he’s brought to the show and his energy and his vibe. … He is a bedrock character on the show.”

Raisani noted that like the 9-1-1 shows that came before Nashville, adding a key character during season 2 is like “adding a major piece to the puzzle” and helps the writers “figure out what we are missing.”

“Ryan really has enhanced our show in a great way. So I definitely see him with us for the long haul,” he teased.

“It’s put on hold while his dad’s missing. He’s not going to leave and, you know, head out of town, so it’s put on hold until there is resolution on that,” Raisani told Us in regards to Ryan taking a break from firefighting to join Sam as she undergoes surgery to battle her cancer and hopefully protect her baby in another state.

He reassured Us that the story will be told and it’s a “pretty big” arc for the married couple.

“[Ryan] is going to step away from the firehouse to be with Sam and and try to get her through this really scary and harrowing journey that she’s on, and they’re going to go through it together,” Raisani said, confirming that the story line will “resolve near the end of the season.”

“She has a very specific reason why she hates Cammie so much,” Raisani explained of 9-1-1 call center supervisor Marcia’s vendetta against worker Cammie, which as of the fall finale has included prank calls and threats of harm virtually.

The showrunner warned that Marcia “means to torment her at the deepest levels, which is part of why she picks the phone is the way to be cruel to Cammie because she identifies with the phone more than any other object to help people.”

Marcia, who has been disguising her voice over the phone and calling Cammie a “hag” while pretending to be a stern but helpful boss at work, is now “tainting” Cammie’s perception of the phone being a lifeline.

“That’s just phase one for what Marcia’s got in store for Cammie,” he teased. “She really does want to take Cammie apart emotionally and mentally, and ultimately physically, and so yes, it’s definitely going to escalate and get more intense.”

He also hinted that Marcia’s young son, who was killed by a drunk driver, could be the key to their connection.

“Right now, Rogue is an obsessive person. It wasn’t his fault, but his first wife died because he was so obsessed with the last serial killer,” Raisani explained. “This is not a guy who’s got, you know, he’s not on Tinder when there’s a serial killer out there.”

He noted, “But the serial killer won’t always be out there, and so I definitely think that will be a fun and rich thing to explore. How this guy starts to date again. We’ll explore that, but just not yet.”

Another day, another dodgy driver: Nvidia's latest driver package (621.24) is needlessly writing to users' SSDs, in some cases by 30 GB every hour. And if that sounds familiar, it's because an issue with Radeon Adrenalin drivers did a similar thing a week ago.

The issue appears to be fairly widespread going from reports on the Nvidia GeForce forum, Dell forum, Super User forum, and many, many threads on Reddit. Though that's a bunch of people that might, and did, notice random writes to their SSD; many more may not visit their task manager to check these things with any regularity.

You can then see how much each process has written, which shouldn't usually be very much at all. I measured my own PC on an older driver version (621.01) and this process had only written 63 MB in an hour of uptime; if you're on the most recent GeForce driver package (621.24), and NVDisplay.Container.exe has a number of gigabytes next to it (it's in bytes, so get your calculator out), you've been bit by the bug.

The affected driver, 621.24, is still available to download right now. That's the surprising thing here, as the issue has seemingly been reported across the internet since November 15; the driver was released on November 12, and it appears to have taken a few days of needlessly huge writes for anyone to notice.

The culprit appears to be a binary log stored at 'C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg'.

This log is being constantly rewritten, rather than appended to, according to the initial report by TroubleGrid. The large file is rewritten each time, therefore it keeps growing over a short period while a PC is switched on; the problem with multiplication like that is repeated multiplication leads to exponential growth. If those writes are sustained around the 1–2 MB/s mark, that's upwards of 5–7 GB/hr, though some users suggest it gets much worse.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The easiest fix is to revert to the previous driver, 621.01 (clean install option on Nvidia installer or use Display Driver Uninstaller first). There is another fix for anyone hoping to keep the latest Game Ready support, as posted by one user on Reddit and generated by Claude. That's a command that changes the Registry to prevent further writes, while retaining functionality of other Game Ready driver features.

What's most surprising here is that the driver is still live on Nvidia's site—it should've been pulled days ago.

#3800. Warren Spector lambasts GTA 6's "billion dollar" development - 'I just hope it's is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer'

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries."

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is."

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he said: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer."

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

A process switch to TSMC N2X is said to be behind the delay.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the company's new Venice range of server chips. Now there's a rumour that the consumer Ryzen chip launch may have been pushed back to the second half of 2027.

The new Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao says otherwise. In a post spotted by Videocardz, Zhang Zhonghao claims that the desktop chips, codenamed Olympic Ridge, have been switched to TSMC's N2X manufacturing process, and as a result the "timeline has been pushed back" (via machine translation).

Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year.

Olympic Ridge was originally though to be using TSMC's N2 or N2P process node, but a switch to the performance-focussed N2X would line up with previous rumours that the chips are targeting very high clockspeeds, potentially all the way up to 6.5 GHz.

N2X is scheduled to enter production in 2027, which would explain the longer timeframe if this rumour proves out. A delay to the second half of next year would mean that Intel's Nova Lake chips, said by the company to be "tracking ahead of schedule" in a recent earnings call, would potentially have the first half of 2026 all to themselves if they launch before Zen 6.

In the battle of the next generation CPUs, Intel would end up with a significant headstart. However, for those thinking about a potential upgrade, it's worth noting that Intel's new chips will use an entirely new socket in the form of LGA 1954. AMD's new offerings will use the existing AM5 socket.

AMD's Jack Huynh posted a cryptic video on X earlier this week, alongside a message declaring that "the next era of computing is going to be special," and that he "can't wait to share a glimpse of what's coming at CES." So, hopefully we might learn more about what's going on with Zen 6 desktop silicon on January 5.
