#3797. Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all."

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

There are some shows on the 2026 TV schedule where I never need to worry if my favorite characters are going to die. That’s very much not the case with Yellowjackets’ impending final season. Tons of key people on the show have already kicked the bucket, and I don’t expect things to slow down before we say goodbye to the series forever. But what do the minds behind the series think about committing make-believe murder on the series so far?

As Yellowjackets fans, we’ve endured everything from Jackie Taylor freezing to death in the Season 1 finale to Van Palmer’s shocking stabbing last season. I asked the show’s creators, Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson, about the hardest death to write so far, and Lyle pointed out one big one she’s not over yet. Here’s what she told CinemaBlend:

One that was really difficult was filming Coach Scott's death. We've had a longstanding friendship and working relationship with Stephen Krueger, and we absolutely love him. And so, it was hard. It was really difficult to say goodbye to that character. But they're all difficult. Every single one of them.

Oof, yeah… Coach’s death was a rough one. Last season, we learned the details of Scott’s demise after the Yellowjackets’ cabin was burned to the ground. Then, he was put on trial by the Yellowjackets, and Shauna ordered Melissa to incapacitate him, which she did by slashing his Achilles tendon. After that, he’s left in agonizing pain and decides to stop eating and essentially begs Natalie to kill him.

Honestly, I totally agree with Lyle here. This was the most difficult death to watch, especially since we saw Coach decline over a number of episodes and felt his impending death coming. I love Yellowjackets, but I have to admit this was a really rough chapter in the series to sit through. While Lyle had to call out Coach’s death, my question wasn’t an easy one to answer. In her words:

They’re all really hard. I mean, because you spend so much time with these characters, and it sounds like such a corny cliché, but like they do kind of start to feel like your children. Like you created them.

On the flip side of things, they’ve already reached the finish line of the series. All that’s left is for us to watch it. Nickerson said it did get easier to kill characters off in the final season, saying this:

The longer you go in the show, I feel like the character is always hard to kill, but at least on a human level, it gets easier because, you know, the show will end eventually. So it's like, again, everybody's gonna need new jobs eventually, right?

Uhh… What does this mean? Who’s going to be safe and who’s going to die? I have no idea (and even the cast was left in the dark about spoilers), but I know I trust the writers to shock, surprise and make me feel a lot of things.

The premiere of Yellowjackets Season 4 airs on Friday, November 20 on SHOWTIME and with a Paramount+ subscription. I’m so curious who will be left standing by the end, and what Melanie Lynskey means by the series getting “crazier” and having a “fun ending”.

#3791. Over 2 million Xbox players in the UK and US reportedly used the 'New Zealand trick' to play GTA 6 early - that's more than a third of the country's population

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the New Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:

Amusingly, New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

Some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3790. Major Esports Tournament Replaced Caster Commentary With AI Voices And It Went Over Very Poorly

Embark Studios, developer of The Finals and organizer of the game’s Grand Major esports tournament, is facing backlash after replacing human casters with AI voices in a highlight reel. IGN reports that the now-deleted video featured footage from the APAC closed qualifiers, but instead of hearing the human casters that actually called the matches, viewers were treated to AI commentators Scotty and June. The incident is rippling through the esports professional community, with some calling for unionization efforts to protect workers.

Proto, one of the casters replaced in the video, spoke out about the incident on social media.

After 4 cycles, open/closed quals, the time, effort, passion and emotion myself @TheeHyperactive and @bluepanda_casts put in. We get replaced by two Ai casters who even quote us :/ I get they are apart of the game but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals https://t.co/oC8Zb5GrU0

— Proto / Kai (@ProtoANZ) November 16, 2026

Oscar Lundberg, community and competitive operations lead at Embark Studios, apologized for video on social media. “We intended for Scotty and June to help bring more casual interest into The Finals esports ahead of TGM,” he wrote. “That was the goal, but the work of our talent deserved to be included and highlighted, and it wasnât.”

The writing was on the wall indicating that something like this would happen in The Finals. When it launched in 2023, The Finals was called out by players for its use of AI text-to-speech voice acting, something the devs have acknowledged and embraced. “AI text-to-speech is finally extremely powerful,” said Andreas AlmstrÃ¶m, the game’s audio director in Embark Studios’ “Meet The Makers” podcast. “It gets us far enough in terms of quality and allows us to be extremely reactive to new ideas.” Earlier this year, The Finals released Dynamic Commentary, a feature that allows the AI commentator to call out players by name whenever something happens during a match.

Dynamic Commentary is the new feature that will earn you praise from your favorite commentator Scotty, coming in PRIME TIME on Oct. 20!

Live commentary in a live match for the play you just pulled. Now this is what a Game Show is all about!â¦ pic.twitter.com/8acAZGY2Zw

— THE FINALS (@reachthefinals) October 18, 2026

It stands to reason that if a developer is comfortable with using AI-text-to-speech to power the game’s in-universe equivalent of esports casting, they might extend that beyond the confines of the game, possibly to see if anyone would notice or care enough about it. Having in-game AI commentary is the inch, this video experiment is the mile. Thankfully esports professionals, many of whom have lost their jobs over the last six years as studio interest and investment has declined, didn’t let this go by unremarked.

In an interview with IGN, Proto spoke about potential organization efforts to prevent something like this from taking hold in the esports community. “I think industry wide, we definitely need to implement some kind of protection for commentary teams as well as production teams,” he said. “You got to protect those people’s jobs.”

I don’t know about you, but my curiosity about Robert Downey Jr. in Avengers: Doomsday just keeps growing. Even though we know he’s under the mask of Doctor Doom, there’s a lot we still don’t know about his role in the newest upcoming Marvel movie. Now, with just a month between us and Doomsday, RDJ got real about where he was at with the MCU before he got the call to join it again.

Downey was revealed to be Doomsday’s Victor von Doom in the summer of 2024, during Marvel’s Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con. It was a huge surprise not only to fans but to the actor, too. As the Oscar winner shared:

I kind of made my peace with it, and it felt so definitive by the time Endgame had been released. When it was first broached by Kevin [Feige], who said, ‘Hey, do you think you would ever?’ And then, I really just thought, ‘How many surprises are left?’

When Avengers: Endgame came out in 2019, it was the end of an era for the MCU. It felt like the franchise had found a great way to wrap up the arc of Tony Stark/Iron Man by having him be the one to save the universe from Thanos. As RDJ said in a new Marvel video, he had made his “peace” with no longer being part of the MCU. But then Marvel president Kevin Feige called.

Recasting the same actor in the same franchise in a different role is pretty unheard of, unless you’re the MCU. It’s the ultimate big move for The Multiverse Saga, and clearly they convinced the actor to rejoin the Marvel family in a whole new way. As Downey Jr. continued:

Any of these movies is only as good as its villain. Victor is a master manipulator, and because of that, there’s levels to the stakes here. It’s such a long bench of talent. These people are people that I would do any movie with eight days a week. We just really keep trying to earn it with every breath. It’s really hard to explain the love I have for this.

Aww, this is sweet. I mean, it’s quite the honor to be asked to play a Marvel villain, especially when it’s one that will assemble just about every character in the universe. It’s wild when you think about it, because the villain that was originally being teased as the big bad of this saga was Kang. However, after Jonathan Majors got caught in some legal trouble, Marvel made a pivot. However, according to recent words from Feige, Doctor Doom was allegedly always in the cards.

And let’s not forget that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers is also set to come back alongside the likes of Chris Hemsworth’s Thor, Paul Rudd’s Ant-Man, Anthony Mackie’s Sam Wilson, Tom Hiddleston’s Loki, and the casts of Fantastic Four: First Steps, Thunderbolts* and the original X-Men movies.

RDJ’s comments certainly make me wonder what we don’t know about Doctor Doom. And I can't wait to learn more about him when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. While we wait, you can catch up on all the Marvel movies and TV shows thus far with a Disney+ subscription.

#3788. Ubisoft cuts jobs at major Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios as its year of layoffs continues

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."

These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" announced by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

World of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Like Rockslicer, an axe that lets you mine ore.

In a recent episode of the official WoW: Forever podcast, senior game designer Aidan Moon spoke a little on his design philosophies, and items that players are yet to see: "There's a lot that they have not seen that I'm very happy with and I think is a great direction for the game."

Moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?'

"That's because, when we say we're a fantasy-forward game, that means that before optimisation, before it being good, it needs to be flavourful, it needs to feel like it belongs in the world and that the stats are essentially a storytelling mechanism for items."

Ultimately, Moon thinks that interesting items that are memorable are far better for the game than a purely optimal numbers upgrade: "I would rather there be an Ogre Loincloth in the game that people talk about and get upset over, than just another strength belt that people go 'oh, that's just the mail strength belt in the dungeon'."

As for what we're yet to get to, Moon, laughing, remarks: "I've done some stupid stuff.

"There may be an item that is master looter BiS—I'll just put it that way … Maybe you get extra stats if your bags are completely full." Finally. An item for people who are allergic to inventory management! Me. I'm talking about myself. My bags are so full please send help.

#3786. GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3785. Detroit Lions Star Aidan Hutchinson Speaks Out After Suffering Shocking Injury

Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is speaking out after suffering a devastating injury.

The athlete, 26, took to Instagram on Thursday, November 19, to share his shock over the incident which will likely end his season prematurely.

“I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me,” Hutchinson wrote as he addressed injuring himself during a sack celebration during a game in Germany on November 15.

Hutchinson vowed not to let the setback get him down, adding, “But even something like this won’t hold me back.”

Hutchinson was injured after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye during Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. The football player jumped into the air in celebration before landing awkwardly on his right leg. ESPN reported on Monday that Hutchinson tore his ACL.

In Thursday’s social media post, the defensive end went on to add that there was no pointing dwelling on why the unexpected situation occurred.

“I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him,” he wrote, thanking fans for their “prayers and well wishes.”

Hutchinson also made it clear that he intends to bounce back, declaring, “I always come back stronger.” Seeing the funny side, he also quipped, “That’s the last time I go airborne 😁👍.”

“Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys,” he added.

Hutchinson’s post comes after the Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell described the loss of the star player as a “gut punch” earlier this week.

“He’s such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he’s an unbelievable teammate and he’s one of our captains,” Campbell said during an appearance on Detroit’s 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, November 17. “It just stinks, man. It hits you. And I hate it for him, man, because he was on a heater.”

Campbell expressed confidence that the defensive star would be able to overcome the obstacle.

“What a hell of a year he was having,” Campbell said. “He’s just improved every year and to come off the injury he had [in 2024]. But I also know this, man: This guy will overcome this and he will come back better than he was, too. It’s just the way he is, it’s the way he’s wired, and he’ll come out better for this.”

Spoilers for the first five episodes of Rings of Power Season 3 are ahead! You can stream the series with an Amazon Prime subscription.

On Rings of Power, we’ve spent seasons trying to figure out the identities of the wizards who were sent to Middle-earth. In Season 2, after we spent a lot of time guessing and theorizing, we learned that The Stranger was indeed Gandalf. However, the identity of the Dark Wizard was still unknown. In Season 3, his true name was finally revealed, though, and I asked the co-creator of the show why they wanted to make the Dark Wizard the Blue Wizard Pallando.

In Episode 3 of the season of Rings of Power that’s currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, Gandalf has an interaction with the Secret Fire, where it’s revealed to him that five wizards were sent to save Middle-earth. That’s how we learned that Pallando, one of the two Blue Wizards, killed his partner, and it’s also when Gandalf learns that he’s been sent to save the corrupted Blue Wizard. When I asked co-creator Patrick McKay why they wanted to make the Dark Wizard Pallando, he began by saying:

Here's the thing that we do on the show: We trust our audience. We're really thinking of it as one 50-hour movie. That's always been the plan and the aspiration. That also means that when we introduce a new character, you might not know where his or her allegiances lie. You might not know his or her name, but we know, and we have a plan.

While the end of Rings of Power Season 2 made me think the Dark Wizard was Saruman (even though that actually makes no sense timeline-wise), the other prevailing theory was that he was a Blue Wizard. Now, it’s confirmed that that’s the case, and McKay told me they made this decision because of how fascinating the lore is behind these two rather mysterious characters:

And you know there is this great lore in Tolkien about the two blue wizards who went east. And Tolkien had different versions of it and different ideas he played with. And a recurrent theme was that maybe one of them went bad, and no one knows what happened to the other one. And then, you know, thinking about that and bringing our wizard, our hero wizard Gandalf, sounds good to say that now, into that story, now you're weaving, right?

At one point, Tolkien wrote that the Blue Wizards could have been “founders or beginners of secret cults and magic traditions that outlasted the fall of Sauron” (via ScreenRant). It’s not confirmed if this is used as inspiration for Rings of Power; however, it does point to the potential moral ambiguity surrounding these magical beings.

On the show, they ultimately decided to run with the notion that Pallando might have done something terrible and killed his partner. Exploring the complexities of that was very interesting to them, as McKay told me:

What might be interesting? Well, gosh, what if Pallando has murdered his partner, and that's where he got his power from, but maybe there's complexity to it. Maybe he has guilt over it. Maybe, you know, he even has a desire for redemption. But how much? And then building a story around that was one of the joys of this season. But you know, the idea of the Blue Wizards is always tantalizing to us as fans, and part of our job is the inner fanboy getting to play.

Well, now I’m certainly excited to see where things go from here. I want to see Gandalf and Pallando interact more. I want to know if Gandalf can help his fellow wizard get away from the evil. And I want to know more about why the Blue Wizard killed his friend.

Hopefully, that will be unveiled as Rings of Power wraps up its third season and releases Episodes 7 and 8 on November 25.

#3783. World of Warcraft: Forever has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years, says Blizzard

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!"

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the new edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players.

#3782. CNN Calls GTA 6 The ‘Most Intense Version Of Pac-Man‘

Folks, I’m not sure if you are aware of this, but video games, like Grand Theft Auto 6, have come a long way since Pac-Man. I’m aware of that, but perhaps the people at CNN might want to play a video game made in the last 20 years.

Today, on CNN, three adults who are paid money to report on the events of the world were asked to talk about the just-launched Grand Theft Auto 6 for a bit, and it was extremely embarrassing and sad for all involved. For some reason, in an effort to explain what GTA 6 is to people who aren’t big gamers, they decided to compare it to Pac-Man. Seriously.

"… think of it as the most intense version of Pac-Man…" – CNN on GTA VI

Come on, man. This industry made over 200 Billion dollars in revenue last year alone. What are we doing here?

— Raj Patel (@rajio.bsky.social) 2026-11-19T21:36:55.884Z

“If you’re not a gamer, think of it as the most intense version of Pac-Man where you are being chased, and you’re chasing with the most lifelike graphics possible.”

Wow! What a terrible way to describe GTA 6. Or really any popular video game made in the last 20 years. Look, I’m not suggesting these people need to be gaming experts. But video games aren’t a tiny niche only played by kids down at the arcade. They’re a massively popular, successful, and influential medium. Some of the biggest shows and movies of the last few years are direct adaptations of games like The Last of Us and Fallout. And GTA 6 is the biggest of the big. You could maybe not waste everyone’s time with such a lazy and useless description.

It’s also just weird because most people on this planet have a basic understanding of what GTA is in 2026. It’s that game where you steal cars and run around and shoot cops. That’s not a perfect description, but it’s much better than the crap CNN is sharing on the air when the network is suddenly forced to talk about video games due to a really, really big one dropping.

Anyway, I can’t wait to be in my 70s and hear reporters in the mainstream media describe GTA 12 or whatever as the best version of Pac-Man you’ve ever seen. Video games really have come a long way, folks…

"I think your BiS should be different every single boss."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"I essentially wanna get rid of [best in slot gear (BiS)]. I think that BiS is not a good thing for a videogame that's supposed to be about roleplaying aspects of it—that's why I've introduced the creature subtype system (where things are more effective against [for example] murlocs), I've introduced a biome system."

"In the raid, it's different … In the raid, if you go to the left wing, that's snowy, if you go to the right wing, that's haunted, if you go down below, that's cavernous. Different parts of the raid will have different biomes. I think your BiS should be different every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," via the official WoW Forever podcast.

I might be going against the grain here, but I'm honestly all for this—my one major hangup, the inventory management, is also swiftly addressed in the podcast, with principal game designer Kris Zierhut commenting that "we've thought about that a lot—it's not something we need right now, but we're going to give you bigger bags and better ways of organising and searching to find those things."

That's my worries solved, then! Moon also chimes in and notes that "Back in Season of Discovery, I think the biggest bags we could give you were 32 slots … now you can make 98-slot bags. I open the bag and my screen just [explodes]."

The major hullabaloo from player communities seems to be this idea that we're just doing resistance gear again. Back in Vanilla WoW, you'd have to farm a bunch of specific elemental resistance gear for specific raids, and it's something that nobody quite like that much.

The way I see this being different, however, is that Moon is very specifically talking about a "theoretical BiS list". In other words, this biome and creature-matching only has to be completely aligned if you want to be maximally sweaty and pump the highest numbers you possibly can.

It does not seem like this gear is mandatory, and I think the actual motivation behind it seems better. Trading off a ton of damage just to get crappy gear pieces so you can survive feels bad, but realising you have the perfect-shaped peg to put into a hole (stop giggling) actually sounds satisfying.

Not that there won't be problems, but I would genuinely rather WoW: Forever try and experiment properly with its gear systems, instead of following the same formula that the main game's been trundling out for the past 20+ years. I am, bare minimum, willing to wait and see how it pans out.

#3780. Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

Just a small warning: There is one spoiler below (about the fate of the dog) for Heart of the Beast, but that’s the only spoiler. If you want to know his fate before watching this, I understand, so I’ve included it here.

Amid all the talk about potential Oscar movies, one film that I actually loved on the 2026 movie schedule that isn’t really getting a lot of attention is Heart of the Beast, starring Brad Pitt. Pitt plays Sergeant Major James Belmont, a retired Special Forces operator, and four different dogs play his trusty companion and fellow war vet, Odin. If you’re wondering, because I know I was, Odin does not die in the movie, so you can rest easy on that front. What Odin does do, along with Pitt, is help deliver a wonderful, heartfelt story that I really want everyone to see.

The story, at its most basic, is a survival one. Belmont and Odin find themselves stranded in the Alaskan bush and must hike miles through the unforgiving wilderness. Really, though, it’s about a man and his dog and what they do for each other, in good times and bad, that the movie is really about. It’s as touching a movie about a friendship as has ever been. Their bond is real, and it is felt from beginning to end.

It isn’t an easy movie to watch, and there are some brutal and intense moments of survival and some carnage to endure. It makes the end so worth it, as the audience, like Belmont, is exhausted. In fact, the moments at the end, some of the most heartbreaking in the movie, come with both sadness and relief after the duo endures to survive. I’m an unabashed Brad Pitt fan, and I think this is some of his best work. It’s also very different from what we often expect from the actor. There is no “coolness” to his character, but there is real strength.

In full transparency, walking into the theater for my screening, I was not looking forward to watching Heart of the Beast. I really debated whether I wanted to see it. Setting aside the possible fate of the dog, I just didn’t know if I wanted to sit through a survival movie, knowing what was sure to come. And I won’t lie, there are some moments I really struggled to watch. I’m not particularly squeamish, but one scene in particular hit way too close to home, and it was tough.

However, it’s worth it! I promise it is. When the lights came up at the end and I started thinking about all that had happened in the movie, it was immensely satisfying. So much so that I really was rooting for it to be a sleeper hit. It wasn’t a huge hit, but it did end up earning just under $200 million over its run at the box office, where it did steady, if not spectacular, business over a few weeks. While Pitt's other movie this year, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, is getting rave early reviews, I hope it doesn't totally overshadow this one.

Heart of the Beast is currently available to buy or rent on VOD, and I urge you to take a chance on it. I think you’ll be surprised just how good it is.

#3778. 'Grey's Anatomy' Star Breaks Silence on [Spoiler]'s Addiction, Show Future

Grey’s Anatomy‘s fall finale came to a shocking end when a main character tried to perform an operation while under the influence — so what does this mean for their future on the show?

During the Thursday, November 19, episode of the hit ABC series, Amelia (Caterina Scorsone) digs into her suspicion that Link (Chris Carmack) has an addiction to painkillers. Her concerns are confirmed when she notices that his pupils are dilated and his hands are shaking during an operation — and she corners him about it with help from Link’s wife, Jo (Camilla Luddington), who doesn’t know what is going on.

“At the end of the midseason finale, Link is really he’s in the crosshairs and he is at a crossroad because Jo obviously is going to find out that something’s going on — unless he can joyfully lie his way out of it, which maybe he can,” Carmack, 45, exclusively told Us.

Carmack pointed out that Amelia “is onto” Link.

“She threw him out of surgery, so he’s going to have to answer on a professional level. There’s going to be repercussions on the personal level. There’s going to be repercussions with Jo,” he continued. “Not to mention, he’s coparenting a child with Amelia. So he’s at the point where there is no way out. He’s going to have to answer for something.”

The actor expressed hope that the revelation doesn’t “tear their family apart,” adding, “It’s going to get rocky, but I would say being thrown out of a surgery because he’s incapable of holding his tools properly is definitely a wake-up call.”

Carmack acknowledged the slow buildup to Link’s substance abuse struggles.

“There are some episodes where it doesn’t really rear its head in terms of telling the story about him getting pills. But I’ve approached the story line from an angle of really denial,” he noted. “He does not believe he has a problem or every step along the way where he kind of recognizes that it might be a problem and it’s getting a little worse. He really thinks he can take care of it himself.”

Carmack continued: “He just sees himself as the guy who has to fix everything, help everyone and be everything to everyone. He’s exhausted, and he has his own trauma from a terrible injury and from the birth of his twins as well, but he’s not facing it. So these drugs, they’ve been numbing not just his physical pain but his mental turmoil.”

Looking ahead, Carmack hinted at how dire the consequences would be for Link — and what it means for his time on the show.

“A question that I was asking our medical supervisors and writers and producers all along has been about the standing of a doctor who’s using pain medications while he’s performing surgeries. The answer that they came up with based on research was that it was a very gray area,” he revealed. “You are allowed to medicate for pain, but of course they can’t be at a place of disability or inability when they’re performing their duties. That’s where I was living with this story line, not thinking he’s going to lose his job because he thinks he has everything under control.”

Link’s job may be in danger, but Carmack hinted that Amelia’s role will create complications, adding, “Amelia going through his medical records is a violation of his personal rights and a violation of HIPAA. Maybe not in a malicious way, but he knows the consequences that she might face.”

Carmack remained largely tight-lipped about the second half of the season but did tease that “there are a lot of secrets being held” by various characters on the show.

You'd think that everyone's favourite character in GTA 6 would be either Jason or Lucia—one of the main characters—but no, another front-runner has emerged for fans: Mandy. She's so much of a favourite, in fact, that we've had to confirm that you can't cheat on Lucia with her.

This still isn't enough to dissuade interest in her for some, as one player proudly announces: "I can fix her". Godspeed soldier, better you than me.

#3776. GTA 6 Is Even Better When You Play It Side-By-Side With Your Wife

Needless to say, there are lots of people out there currently playing Grand Theft Auto 6, and despite what a lot of headlines and social media jokes insist, itâs not solely a boysâ club. Perhaps more than any other GTA game before it, the latest title attracts all kinds of people, and some of these people happen to be couples living in the same houseâmirroring GTA 6âs protagonists just a little bit.

My partner, who has not played a Grand Theft Auto game before, and I have both been excited to lay our hands on GTA 6, and stayed up late last night for the midnight unlock time. But unlike most in our situation, we neither passed the controller back and forth nor went to different rooms to enjoy our games separately. See, because I am an insane person, I have a setup that lets us both start the game simultaneously.

Obviously, both my partner and I are game journalists, and both of us have worked in this industry for many years. When we first started living together, after she moved to San Francisco to join IGN, I foresaw a situation in which we would both have to review games at the same time. Maybe, then, it would make sense for us to have setups that allowed us to play different consoles simultaneously, maybe in different rooms or parts of the same room.

âWhy not just put them next to each other?â she posited as we mentally planned out our apartment. Why not, indeed!

That birthed what visiting friends all point out is a truly odd setup, but one that occasionally pays dividends. In the setup, we have my TV on the left and her TV on the right. The consoles on the left side are mine and only hook into my TV, while the consoles on the right side do the same to her TV, with the PC in the middle duplicating the image to both. Usually one person will wear headphones if weâre both playing something.

This works out well with a lot of games. When we were playing through Elden Ring before release side-by-side, one of us would occasionally look at the other’s screen, not recognize where the other person was, and so weâd share notes on how to get there. When Tears of the Kingdom launched at midnight, an informal race to get all the shrines motivated us to solve puzzles in more interesting ways than the other person.

With Grand Theft Auto 6, though, it allowed us to see exactly what little details were changing in the game depending on our different actions and approaches.

In the gameâs prologue, Lucia tries her best to make it back to a coffee shop while the police search for her, scouring the city block. Since itâs mere minutes after the opening of the game, my partner and I got there at roughly the same time. She, pragmatic as she is, chose to walk along the sidewalks until the cops eventually picked her up. I tried to cut around the building and swim, and then I got hit in the head by a police boat and was knocked unconscious. Whoops.

For me, in the cutscene that followed, Lucia was being handcuffed to a gurney while EMS and police pushed her into the back of an ambulance. For my partner, Lucia was being manhandled by police into the back of a cop car. In both situations, she pleaded about needing to go back to the coffee shop, but it was maybe a bit more fraught and scary in my case as she fought to maintain consciousness.Â

The scenes were similar, but different, and it was fascinating to be able to watch them side-by-side like this. That wow factor has kind of kept up throughout as we’ve continued playing. In an early mission, I watched her, playing as Jason, enter a car impound lot in a completely different way than I had. She gave me tips about when I would be able to play as Lucia, noticing that I was bumming around a lot (to which I answered, âBut I have to make sure sheâs happy with the house first.â)Â

I wonder if Iâm signing up for a lifetime of doing more chores without realizing it.

We’re planning to play the bulk of the rest of the game like this; it probably won’t surprise anyone that we have a lot of TVs around the house and sometimes I move consoles around to play things in my office. But our setup is interesting, and it lets us spend time together while still partaking in hobbies that we love. Tonight weâre both going to continue playing GTA while I set up a laptop on the coffee table to watch the episode of AEW Dynamite that we missed yesterday, and that might be pushing it a little bit. Or maybe three screens is the perfect number?

#3775. Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises."

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever."

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

#3774. Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

"BIS is not a good thing for a game that's supposed to be about role-playing."

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different."

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list."

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

There is no shortage of drama when it comes to the Mormon Wives franchise.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, which is available with a Hulu subscription, was an instant sensation. It shone a spotlight on the success and scandals of its O.G. cast, including the drama prone Taylor Frankie Paul. Because of that attention, it felt like a given that producers would want to do a spinoff, which led to the recent debut of an Orange County, Calif. version centered around Jen Affleck on the 2026 TV schedule.

The new series has a mix of faith-based Mormons alongside women who either seem to be taking a break from the Church or just don’t want anything to do with it at all, which of course is going to lead to some friction. When clashes escalate, viewers can’t help but notice, and executive producer Jeff Jenkins got worried that the cast might not make it through the season. He told The Wrap that while they ended the season in a better place, it was questionable for a minute:

There’s still friggin’ potholes of disagreement, but I think they end stronger as a group than when they began. I didn’t even know if they were going to make it through week one. Honestly, I was like, ‘Oh my god, these girls are going to murder each other.’

He's likely joking about the whole "murder" thing, but having seen the Hulu reality series, I get where the sentiment comes from. The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is comprised of two groups that former Dancing with the Stars contestant Affleck wants to bring together – the “Molly Mormons,” who are all-in on their faith, and the “Jack Mormons,” who either more loosely follow the teachings or have left it behind entirely. That can be a challenge in any setting, so it was not surprising when the tension between Mayci Neeley’s older sister McCall DePron and internet personality Bobbi Althoff became more heated.

The good news is that the Mormon Wives: OC cast genuinely does seem to have ended in a better place than they started, and no murder has actually been committed. When you’re just getting to know each other and feeling out what someone’s boundaries are, clashes are bound to happen, especially when you have some different viewpoints and perspectives. It’s what you do once you know a person better that matters. And Bobbi even publicly posted on Instagram Stories to ask people to stop bullying McCall, as they worked out their own differences. Here’s what she had to say, in her own words:

A post shared by The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives News & Updates (@secretlivesupdates)

Largely because of Taylor Frankie Paul, the original The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives series has had its fair share of chaos surrounding production. After the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette and custody issues with her children, the MomTok star announced that she was leaving the show. Things haven’t gone that far with anyone in the Orange County spinoff.

Sure, they have some personal drama, from Jen Affleck deciding she wants to follow through with a divorce while pregnant with her fourth child, and Aspyn Ovard publicly showing what her life is like as part of a throuple. Bobbi even admitted to signing on for the heightened visibility reality TV brings. They also seem to genuinely want to be there as a support system for Jen and are willing to give each other grace through the mistakes and missteps.

While waiting to hear about whether there will be a Season 2 for the Orange County cast and the status of the original series seems a bit unclear, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show. It will certainly be interesting to see how things play out for all of these women, and hopefully they will continue to not murder each other.

Let's hope we actually see some performance gains from it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

OpenAI has recently reported that its frontier models attempted to rewrite AMD circuits and received an up-to 14% PPA (Power, Performance and Area) boost. OpenAI says these rewrites are "production-viable" too (via BigGo Finance).

The claim is not that humans couldn't make these same optimisations, but instead that it did around a year's worth of design optimisations in less than 5 months, an optimisation of optimisation, if you will. (Okay, I'll stop writing optimisation now.)

Apparently, AMD has even incorporated some of these findings into chip designs that have recently gone to manufacturing. The model worked on an in-house "Jalapeño" chip, as well as an AMD "flagship GPU IP" and "AMD next-gen flagship CPU key modules." Each one of these saw different gains.

For the Jalapeño vector compute unit, the model's changes managed to reduce cell area by around 13%, and this was observed when powering on the hardware. The Jalapeño compute unit saw the standard cell area reduced by around 10%, with the multiplier area alone reduced by around 15 % and latency cut from two clock cycles to one.

It's the AMD flagship GPU that saw the 14% PPA improvement, and AMD has reportedly verified a 'single-digit' PPA improvement on the next-gen CPU.

Using a budget of around 112,000 tokens, all models in the report (GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-5.6 Sol) performed better when asked to design a RISC-V core from scratch, rather than optimising one given to them. That being said, OpenAI does note that models asked to entirely redesign rather than optimise could omit features in the original design, which can become its own problem.

Generative AI is a bit of a double-edged sword in the PC hardware space. Before mentioning the memory crisis the AI global buildout is responsible for, generative AI's ability to work constantly and fast can be a boon for development, but it can also be a slog to work through. Linux engineers are currently struggling to get on top of the thousands of bugs AI is finding, which is a real monkey's paw element of the tech. And it's a sign that AI itself needs to be maintained and monitored, even if it genuinely does seem to produce favourable results in engineering.

#3770. 'Grey's Anatomy' Reveals Major Health Scare as [Spoiler]'s Legs Stop Working

Grey’s Anatomy ended its season 23 fall finale on a cliffhanger after a main character suffered a health scare when their legs stopped working.

During the Thursday, November 19, episode of the hit ABC show, Wes (Trevor Jackson) surprised Simone (Alexis Floyd) by breaking up with her. They didn’t have much time to talk until the end of their shifts when he came to apologize. Things took a turn, however, when Wes collapsed because his legs stopped working and he said he could no longer feel them.

This surprise story line comes after Wes revealed he had CVID (common variable immunodeficiency) and the condition prevented him from being able to get vaccinated. He was placed on leave after coming in contact with a patient with measles and wasn’t able to return to the hospital for 28 days while they waited to see if he would develop symptoms.

Simeone, meanwhile, had a difficult season as well after thinking she was pregnant. She chose to terminate her pregnancy, but there were complications, so Simone had to go through a dilation and curettage (D&C), a procedure where the cervix is dilated in order to remove tissue from inside the uterus. (The procedure is commonly used for abortions and to treat missed or incomplete miscarriages.)

It remains to be seen how Wes’ emergency will affect his future on the show. Grey’s Anatomy has had its fair share of shakeups this season with an even more limited number of episodes. The medical drama previously had as many as 27 episodes per season, but this year, there are only 13.

“But even in the last two seasons with what you saw this year, we had to reduce the cast a little bit [because of industry-wide budget cuts], and everybody has very passionate feelings about their favorite characters,” executive producer Meg Marinis told The Hollywood Reporter in May 2025. “But if we can get the writers upset then we know we’re doing it right. It’s not as satisfying a story if people aren’t upset when someone leaves. It’s supposed to make people upset and sad, so I’m sure there’ll be some arguments. But I’ve been persuaded before to change my mind on things.”

Despite the major changes, Marinis is holding out hope that some former cast members might find a way to return this season.

“I hope so! We love bringing former cast [members] back when they’re available and it makes sense story-wise,” she told The Hollywood Reporter in October. “We have some ideas percolating, so I’m hopeful we’ll have some fun nostalgic surprises for fans this season.”

Grey’s Anatomy is streaming on Hulu and returns Thursday, January 7.

#3769. Here’s What People Are Playing That’s Not GTA 6

Yes, GTA 6. Biggest game of the generation. You feel every penny and hour that went into making it, very good. But there are dozens, dozens! of people out there who, because of a lack of an appropriate platform, funds, or simply interest, are not playing this game at all. I wanted to hear from them, so I posted a call on Bluesky, “Hey, tell me what you’re playing that’s not GTA 6.” Here’s a summary of what I heard.

Queen’s Domain came up early and often as a GTA 6 alternative. In fact, perusing my thread, it was the game that came up the most. I don’t know anything about the game (and I plan on fixing that as soon as possible) but what I’ve gather so far is…this is a game about holes. I found this quote from Derek Liu particularly illuminating for that game’s whole deal. “Queenâs Domain is great for ‘I wonder if thereâs anything at the bottom of this hole?’ style of exploration.”

WoW Forever was another high-volume contender, as was the Ocarina of Time remake which has somehow tripped me up at the Water Temple even though I’ve been told it’s been nerfed from its original difficulty 30 years ago. And shout out to the people who are still in part one of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, you are real and you are valid (and you are also me).

Fortune's Weave is so long man I'm still on part 1

— SinÃ©ad McDevitt (@neadiegirl.bsky.social) 2026-11-18T16:21:18.229Z

Speaking of “things that are me,” I have to mention all the homies participating in a Warhammer game of some stripe. So far in my quest to sample every genre of Warhammer game, I’ve gotten around to Warhammer Survivors, Rogue Trader, and Space Marine 2. The only genre I haven’t touched yet (I think) are the strategy games and I’m in luck that Dawn of War IV will be out at the end of the month.

Dawn of War 4 comes out November 30th. I am more hype for that than GTA 6 because moving soldiers around on a map is still the most pure form of gaming

— Willie Dustice (@williedustice.bsky.social) 2026-11-18T20:08:15.124Z

So many cozy indies got a mention too, including Milki Delivery, Tanuki: Pon’s Summer, and of course Dressmaker (which will be featured during AGDQ 2027 and I’m excited to see how a dressmaking game can be speedrun.)

The way that GTA 6 is dominating every airwave and will continue to do so for at least a few weeks longer is probably isolating for folks who don’t have any interest in that game. It is the game of the moment and deserves this level of discussion, as tedious as it can be sometimes. But I wanted to make a space for folks to have a different discussion, and I was surprised at how swift and voluminous of a response I got. I wanted to share that here, to break up the GTA 6 stream for just a little bit.

So tell us, what are you playing that’s not GTA 6? Let us know in the comments below.

It's an exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Because after the VisionQuest finale brought back Wanda Maximoff, we're just a month away from the next upcoming Marvel movie with Avengers: Doomsday. Fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are expecting big things from the crossover event, especially with The Russo Brothers back behind the camera. Anthony Mackie will be back as Sam Wison/ Captain America, and dropped a 10-word description about what the blockbuster is about.

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is very limited, which is why there are so many theories and rumors swirling around the internet. Mackie is part of the ensemble Doomsday cast list, which will see multiple teams of heroes unite to battle Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. In a clip from the podcast Happy Sad Confused's Instagram, the Hurt Locker actor was asked to describe the movie, and he responded with:

It’s a day full of a lot of fucking Doom.

Points were made. Marvel's security is notoriously tight, so the 48 year-old actor isn't able to share much ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's release in December. So while the above comments didn't reveal any new information, it's a funny way of describing the forthcoming battle against the villainous title character. Luckily the wait is nearly over for its release in theaters.

This clip arrived online shortly after Anthony Mackie seemingly spoiled Paul Bettany appearing in Doomsday. He has since defended those viral comments, but clearly fans are dissecting every comment made about the mysterious Avengers flick. So perhaps keeping future teases brief is the smartest movie in the final weeks of press.

Stakes are always high for the Avengers movies, and the next one is no exception. We haven't seen the team of heroes together since Infinity War and Endgame, which resulted in the death of beloved characters like Iron Man, Black Widow, and more. Because of this, fans are nervous about which characters might not make it out alive this time around. As a reminder, you can re-watch Doomsday's trailer below.

Anticipation Avengers: Doomsday has reached a fever pitch, with fans desperate for information about what's to come, and what surprise characters might pop up. Kevin Feige teased that more heroes will appear outside of the initial cast list, which was proven right when Chris Evans' Steve Rogers got his own trailer. Now fans are expecting to see Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch, and there's not telling who might appearing during its mysterious runtime. The stakes are sky high, and Mackie's comments, albeit brief, drive that home.

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. The wait is nearly over, so we'll see if the blockbuster hits theaters without anything (else) being spoiled.
